name.text: Relations Q2 - Mapping type for f(x) = x squared

questiontext.text: Consider the function f(x) = x2 for all real numbers. What type of mapping does this function represent?

generalfeedback.text:
To classify the mapping, check whether different inputs can give the same output. Try x = 2 and x = negative 2. Both give f(x) = 4. So two different inputs, 2 and negative 2, map to the same output, 4. This pattern repeats for every nonzero input and its negative.

Since many inputs share the same output, the mapping is many-to-one. It cannot be one-to-many or many-to-many, because each input still gives only one output. It is also not one-to-one, since we just found two inputs sharing an output. The correct answer is B.

questionvariables.text: options2: ["A. One-to-many","B. Many-to-one","C. One-to-one","D. Many-to-many"]; tans2: "B. Many-to-one";
